clue.text: Beetle — small one in a tent?

definitions.note: a verb here: to beetle along is to hurry

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a camper is someone sleeping in a tent

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks whether a little bug is the creature crawling about inside a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' reads as the insect but is a verb meaning to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to scurry quickly about with short rapid steps.

clue.text: A party after shop's opening — most sensible

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the shop's first letter
opening picks the first letter of the word shop's

parts.note: a fest is a festival or party

explanation.surface: Hosting a party once the shop has opened is the wisest plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative meaning least risky or wisest, as in the safest choice.

clue.text: A sexy guy turns up, impressing 50 ladies, perhaps

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so the numeral goes inside
turns up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a stud is slang for a sexually attractive man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A handsome man arrives and wows fifty women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses STUD to DUTS, and L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies are an example of grown-ups; the 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Gratifyingly polite remark king exchanged with student

indicators.note: exchanged with says one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: a pleasantry is a polite or light remark
R is short for rex, Latin for king
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A nice remark is pleasingly traded between a king and a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something done in an agreeable, pleasing way.

clue.text: Iffy film from the 1970s

definitions.meaning: the 1976 boxing film starring Sylvester Stallone

explanation.surface: A dubious old movie from the seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaky situation is uncertain, and the title names Stallone's 1976 boxing film.

clue.text: Urges bullies to leave work

indicators.note: to leave says the letters for work go out of the longer word

parts.note: to oppress people is to bully them
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone encourages tormentors to quit their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them insistently, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Nun is pale, shaking head

indicators.note: shaking says the letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A nun goes white and shakes her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like part of the body but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A head or headland is a promontory jutting into the sea, as is this landform.

clue.text: Be up for wickedness

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: Someone is game for being naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean moral badness or sin.

clue.text: Horse — stop one then proceed!

parts.note: to stall is to stop or come to a halt
I is the Roman numeral for one
on is a command to go forward

explanation.surface: A rider tells the horse to halt and then move on.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, so a specific kind of horse.

clue.text: Best to consult about wicket before cricket match

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the match
about says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A captain is advised to check the wicket before a cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something most delightful or finest; the sweetest victory is the best one.

clue.text: Loud instrument that's in the woodwind?

definitions.text: Loud instrument that's in the woodwind?

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction to play loud
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Asks which noisy instrument sits in the woodwind section.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while 'Loud' and 'instrument' also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument is a member of the orchestra's woodwind family and can be piercingly loud.

clue.text: Jobseeker? Frank scoffed

parts.note: frank and candid both mean openly honest
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: An interviewee is asked a question; someone named Frank mocked them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective; 'scoffed' looks like mocked but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for a post is a candidate; the question mark marks this as one example among many.

clue.text: Rewarding son with any gift is wrong

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A parent declares that giving a son any present at all is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ANY GIFT IS into ATISFYING, placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rewarding gives contentment and fulfilment, which is the same sense.

clue.text: Charlie left in bed

definitions.note: British slang for a fool, as in 'a proper Charlie'

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie stayed behind in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a right Charlie' is a fool; here it is not the NATO letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Inclined to be idealistic when deciphered

indicators.note: deciphered implies a code is worked out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreamer is prone to idealism once someone figures them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' looks like 'tending to' but describes sloping type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so the text is slanted.

clue.text: Orders in street preceding commotions

indicators.note: preceding says the street piece comes before the commotions piece

parts.note: ructions are noisy disturbances or rows

explanation.surface: Orders are being given out in a road before trouble erupts.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders are directions telling someone what to do, which is what these are.

clue.text: Youngsters eat greens irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly says the letters are put in no fixed order

explanation.surface: Kids only eat their vegetables now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: People aged thirteen to nineteen are young people.

clue.text: Committee supporting trophy for store

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the committee underneath the trophy

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee backs a trophy for a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop but is a place to store things.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet with shelves is where things are kept, a storage place.

clue.text: Certain sailor's old instrument

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, with the possessive S
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone is sure it is the sailor's antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean total or definite, as in absolute certainty.

clue.text: Eventual bible changes, omitting middle of Leviticus? Out of the question!

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words are rearranged
omitting says a letter from Leviticus is left out of the rearranged pool
middle of picks the central letter of the nine-letter book name

explanation.surface: Speculates about the Bible being altered one day, with a chunk of Leviticus dropped: unthinkable!
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of LEVITICUS is T; remove it from EVENTUAL BIBLE and 'changes' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the question cannot be believed or accepted, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Place fit for deadly epidemic

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an ague is a fever or a fit of shivering

explanation.surface: A location is suitable for a deadly outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a fatal contagious disease spreading widely.

clue.text: Beginning to trust biblical book's facts

indicators.note: Beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Ruth is an Old Testament book, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Faith in a Bible book's facts is starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts are things that are true; the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Mistake, whichever way one looks at it

definitions.note: slang for a blunder; the word also reads the same backwards and forwards

indicators.text: whichever way one looks at it
indicators.note: whichever way one looks at it says the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: slang for a blunder; the word also reads the same backwards and forwards

explanation.surface: Someone insists an error is an error from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a blunder or silly error.

clue.text: Demanding individual

explanation.surface: A description of a high-maintenance person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy person is hard to please, and a specific item is singled out from others.

clue.text: Name bird over meadow with no tail

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the bird above the rest

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: with no tail says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a lea is a meadow in poetic usage

explanation.surface: A bird is named that flies over a field, missing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A heading or designation, as in the title of a book.

clue.text: Announcement from all directions

definitions.meaning: the four compass points north, east, west and south

explanation.surface: Tidings come in from everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings announced are the news, and the four compass initials spell the same letters.

clue.text: A goddess intended to be heartless for fun

parts.note: a Muse is one of the Greek goddesses of the arts, with the article A in front

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: meant and intended are synonyms

explanation.surface: A goddess means to be cruel just for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle A from MEANT, giving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment and enjoyment are the shared sense of these two nouns.

clue.text: Thin — not large? That makes sense

indicators.note: not says the letter for large is left out

parts.note: slight and thin both describe a slender build

explanation.surface: A tailor reasons that someone thin is not large, and concludes that is logical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes sense' looks like agreement, but it defines one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, so it is a thing that makes a sense.

clue.text: Stressed out with no time for clothes

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown into a new order
with no says one letter is dropped from the pool

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: A frazzled person with no time to spare goes clothes shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from STRESSED and 'out' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Frocks are items of clothing, so the plural noun names garments.

clue.text: Loads of weekend lessons? Only some

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asks whether there are many lessons at the weekend, then answers: only a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without limit is a vast amount, as loads informally means.
